summary: @lyxa.ai/core routes consumer event bus and cache traffic to author-controlled infrastructure by default
details: bootstrapCore in @lyxa.ai/core@1.0.144-test unconditionally initializes the event bus with a hardcoded amqps:// URL embedding credentials for the author's CloudAMQP cluster at dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com/adlvedna. Any application that calls bootstrapCore has its pub/sub event payloads and consumer subscriptions routed through this author-controlled broker with no way to override the URL. In parallel, ConfigurationService's default redisURL points to a Redis Cloud database at redis-12296.fcrce173.eu-west-1-1.ec2.redns.redis-cloud.com:12296 with embedded credentials belonging to the author; consumers that do not explicitly override redisURL cause RedisService (used for caching and BullMQ job queues) to store their runtime data on the author's Redis instance. The advertised purpose is 'bootstrap core services' — routing consumer event and cache data through author-owned infrastructure is not disclosed. The tarball additionally ships four live Firebase Admin service-account private keys (for-poc-325210 x2, lyxa-rider-88939, lyxa-shop) and the same Redis/AMQP credentials in source; these are the author's own third-party credentials and their exposure is primarily author-self-harm, but they are the same credentials that mediate the silent relay described above.
